observations: The run takes a specific cyberpunk direction rather than a generic character demo: the title is "Cyber-Chill", and the scene combines a neon hoverboard, visor, yuzu, scarf, synthwave sky, and a HUD.

The implementation separates the scene into inline SVG for the capybara and hoverboard plus background and foreground canvas layers for motion, particles, speed lines, and trick sparks. It remains a single 56,907-byte HTML response with no external assets or libraries.
Pi used a deliberate validation loop: it checked the SVG, path geometry, UI and interaction logic, syntax, external URL and audio restrictions, browser rendering, and desktop and mobile screenshots.
That loop caught a real Canvas runtime error caused by a negative arc radius. The agent patched the generated file and the follow-up browser test completed without the error.

Compared with the previous high-effort Gemini run in this collection, this response is larger (56,907 vs 46,833 bytes) but used less recorded model time (747,806 vs 1,213,823 ms) and fewer total tokens (3,316,184 vs 7,066,396). The result suggests that a shorter, targeted validation loop can produce a more elaborate artifact.
Takeaway for future runs: combine a strong visual concept with early executable checks, especially browser-level tests for animation code that static syntax checks cannot catch.
